mechanism: %match-multisig (src/validation/solver.lisp:120-149) requires (<= #x51 (aref script 0) #x60) for m and the same byte range at script[len-2] for n, so both counts must be an OP_1..OP_16 opcode, and the guard (<= 1 m n 16) repeats the ceiling. Core's MatchMultisig (refs/bitcoin/src/script/solver.cpp:84-105 at d3056bc) reads BOTH numbers through GetScriptNumber(opcode, data, min, MAX_PUBKEYS_PER_MULTISIG) (:66-83), which accepts OP_1..OP_16 through DecodeOP_N OR any minimally-encoded data push (IsPushdataOp + CheckMinimalPush + CScriptNum with fRequireMinimal), and only then range-checks against [min, 20]. 17..20 have no OP_n opcode, so Core reaches them exactly through the push arm: for 17 the script carries 0x01 0x11, CheckMinimalPush passes because data[0] > 16 (script.cpp:373), and CScriptNum yields 17, inside [1,20]. Core therefore classifies bare 17-of-n through 20-of-20 as TxoutType::MULTISIG; we classify them :nonstandard. The upper bound agrees at 21 (Core's max is MAX_PUBKEYS_PER_MULTISIG = 20) and the minimality rule agrees below 17 (a 1-byte push of 2 or 3 is non-minimal for Core and unmatched by us).
consequence: are-inputs-standard-p (src/validation/transaction.lisp:615-643) returns NIL for any prevout classify-script calls :nonstandard, so this node refuses to relay a transaction spending a bare 17..20-key multisig output that Core relays: Core's AreInputsStandard (refs/bitcoin/src/policy/policy.cpp:213-248) rejects only NONSTANDARD and WITNESS_UNKNOWN, and MULTISIG passes. The same misclassification reaches every RPC that reports a script type through bl.val:script-type-name -- getblock verbosity 2/3 and decoderawtransaction/getrawtransaction via output-to-json (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:516-518), gettxout (:724), decodescript (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:422), /rest/ (src/rpc/rest.lisp:268, :615) and the PSBT decoder (src/wallet/psbt.lisp:168) -- all of which say "nonstandard" where Core says "multisig". It is a policy divergence only, not consensus: such an output is non-standard to CREATE (bare-multisig-standard-p caps n at 3, Core IsStandard policy.cpp:85-93), so it can only reach the chain through a miner, which is why this stays S3 rather than S2. Nothing is unspendable -- a miner can still include our refused spend.

No Core unit test pins the 17..20 case; script_standard_tests.cpp:65-89 pins 1-of-2 and 2-of-3 as MULTISIG and :176-194 pins the degenerate shapes (0/2, 2/1, n=2 with 1 key, n=1 with 0 keys) as NONSTANDARD, so the divergent range is unpinned on both sides.
fix_shape: Port GetScriptNumber rather than widening the opcode range. Add a helper that takes a script position and returns (values count next-pos) for either an OP_1..OP_16 opcode or a minimally-encoded push -- minimality is Core's CheckMinimalPush, so a 1-byte push whose value is 1..16 or 0x81 must be rejected, an empty push must be OP_0, and a push of at most 75 bytes must use the direct-length opcode -- then apply CScriptNum's minimal decode and the [min,max] range test with max = 20 (a new +max-pubkeys-per-multisig+ constant next to the existing consensus use, so the two cannot drift). %match-multisig then reads m with min 1 and n with min m, both capped at 20, keeps the existing key-push walk between them, and keeps requiring that the n push ends exactly at len-2. Note Core's MatchMultiA (solver.cpp:106-139) uses the same helper for a threshold up to 999, so the helper is worth exporting even though our solver has no multi_a arm today. The regression test must include the agreement cases as controls -- 21 keys and a non-minimal encoding of 3 must stay :nonstandard -- otherwise a widened range would pass vacuously.
